summary: Extracted the political domain (government, factions, court/authority structure, trial procedure, executioner, Duchess's standing, diplomatic relations) from structured_story + events.json for all 12 source chapters. Wrote factions[2], offices[8], laws[5], relationships[1] to bible/politics.json, keeping the existing _meta id_prefixes/entry_schema and updating status to phase2_draft_pending_merge.

cross_domain_assumptions.note: The source's literal 'living playing-card' court (flat, two-dimensional, card-shaped soldiers/courtiers/gardeners; Knave 'made entirely of cardboard') is modelled here as a human household in Hearts-suit livery/heraldry for faction/office purposes only. Final visual/physical treatment is p2-magic's SUP-* call (bible/cultivation.json); if it differs, only emblem_visual/summary text needs updating, not the office/law structure.

Court institutions described as internally consistent regardless of whether the dream frame is kept literal, ambiguous, or reinterpreted as real (that's world/magic-cultivation's call); no political entry depends on the answer.

Uses the Gryphon's on-page reveal (ch009, 'they never executes nobody') as the interpretive key: the Queen's rule is read as performative/theatrical terror, not literal bloodless beheadings. This is a faithful source-grounded reading (not an invention) but is load-bearing for LAW-001 and the FAC-house-of-hearts summary, so it is flagged explicitly.

OFF-003 (executioner) records only the procedural/jurisdictional dispute over the disembodied Cheshire Cat head (ch008), not how the Cat's head itself is rendered — that belongs to 04-creatures / p2-magic SUP-*.

Source names no neighbouring nation or rival court; the House of Hearts is treated as a single isolated micro-polity (a walled estate). 'Diplomatic relations' in this file are therefore internal (crown vs. subordinate household) rather than international — no external polity was invented to fill a gap that doesn't exist in the source.

known_cross_ref_risks_for_merge.risk: References LOC-hearts-estate and LOC-duchess-house in bible/geography.json, which is still skeleton_empty (02-worldbuilding/geography runs in parallel). These are this agent's best-guess, source-grounded slugs, marked inferred:true with reason. memory-bible's cross_refs_valid_all_namespaces check must reconcile against geography's actual LOC-* registry at merge and return a conflict to this agent (02-worldbuilding/political) if the slugs do not match — per SOUL.md boundary, this agent does not create LOC-* entries itself.

Schema calls for TL-*/ERA-* refs from bible/timeline.json, which is also still skeleton_empty in parallel. Left as an empty array; the phase-by-phase chapter record is instead carried in relationships[].phases (chapter-cited, resolvable now) so no political fact is blocked. memory-bible should backfill period once bible/timeline.json lands.

CHAR-* is forward-reference whitelisted per WRITE_RULES.md section 4. Used predictable slugs (CHAR-king-of-hearts, CHAR-queen-of-hearts, CHAR-duchess, CHAR-white-rabbit, CHAR-bill-the-lizard, CHAR-knave-of-hearts) expected to align with 03-characters/character-manager's naming; not yet verifiable since bible/characters/index.json is still skeleton_empty.

deliberately_unrevealed_in_source: OFF-003 (Royal Executioner) holders left empty: the source never names this character, referring to him only as 'the executioner' (ch008#p61-p71). Recorded as deliberately unrevealed, not a placeholder gap.

The verdict of the tart-theft trial (LAW-004) is never reached in the source; the trial is interrupted by the flying pack of cards and Alice's waking (see story/events.json broken_chains on ev0052). Recorded as unresolved-by-source, not a placeholder gap.

How the Duchess's death sentence (ch008) was lifted before her reappearance free in ch009 is never shown (see story/events.json broken_chains on ev0039); recorded as an unexplained-in-source narrative gap within FREL-001's phase notes, not invented.
no_unknown_placeholder_self_check: PASS - grepped all string values for UNKNOWN/unknown/TBD/N/A; only hit was the literal 'chNNN' template token inside _meta.entry_schema (documentation, not a real entry) and citation-format text, which is expected and not a violation.
cross_ref_self_check: PASS (internal) - all offices[].faction_ref, laws[].issued_by, relationships[].from/to resolve within this file; all entry IDs unique; FAC-* slugs match ^FAC-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; all chapter citations fall within ch001-ch012 per story/chapter_manifest.json.
world_faction_table_alignment: NOT YET VERIFIABLE - bible/world.json is still skeleton_empty (owned by 02-worldbuilding/world, running in parallel; world.json's own scope note states faction detail belongs to this file, politics.json, so no FAC-* table is expected on world's side to diff against yet). This file's FAC-* entries (FAC-house-of-hearts, FAC-duchess-household) are the authoritative faction registry for the project per WRITE_RULES.md section 4 cross-reference table. Flagging for p2-merge to confirm world.json does not independently register overlapping factions.
